fullPassage:
You are the narrator of your own life. The tone and perspective with which you describe each experience generates feelings associated with that narration. For example, if you find yourself constantly assuming, “This is hard,” “I wonder whether I’m going to survive,” or “It looks like this is going to turn out badly,” you’ll generate (a) anxious feelings. It’s time to restructure the way you think. Underlying this narration are the beliefs that (b) frame your experience and give it meaning. Think of your beliefs as having many layers.
On the surface are your automatic thoughts. These are like short tapes that momentarily flash through your mind. Call these automatic thoughts a form of “self-talk” that you use as you navigate through the day. You (c) produce a wide variety of these automatic thoughts, some consciously and some unconsciously. For example, automatic thoughts that (d) relieve anxiety go something like this: You walk into a room, see a few new people, and say to yourself, “Oh, no, I don’t like this. This is not good.” Or, “These people will soon find out that I am full of anxiety and will reject me.” Automatic thoughts are bad habits that (e) cloud fresh and positive experiences. They can turn a potentially good experience into one fraught with anxiety. If you tell yourself that you are always stressed or full of anxiety before doing something new, that new experience will be tainted by that anxiety.

questions.passage: You are the narrator of your own life. The tone and perspective with ①<u>which</u> you describe each experience ②<u>generates</u> feelings associated with that narration. For example, if you find yourself constantly ③<u>assuming</u>, “This is hard,” you’ll generate anxious feelings. It’s time to restructure the way you ④<u>think</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 모두 어법상 올바르다. ① which: 전치사+관계대명사, ② generates: 주어 tone and perspective 단수취급, ③ assuming: find+목적어+~ing, ④ think: the way (that) you think
det.analysis:
✅ 모두 올바름 — 이 문제에서 오류는 없음. 어법 확인 문제.
참고: ② generates에서 주어가 ‘The tone and perspective’로 복합 주어지만 원문에서 단수 동사를 사용.
det.tip: 전치사+관계대명사: with which, in which, by which 형태 숙지

questions.passage: On the surface are your automatic thoughts. These are like short tapes that ①<u>momentarily</u> flash through your mind. You produce a wide variety of these automatic thoughts, some ③<u>conscious</u> and some unconsciously. They can turn a ④<u>potentially</u> good experience into one fraught with anxiety.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ conscious → consciously: some consciously and some unconsciously와 병렬 구조를 이루려면 부사 형태가 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ③ conscious: 원문은 consciously(부사). 병렬 구조(some ___ and some ___ly)에서 부사가 필요
✅ ① momentarily: 부사로 올바름
✅ ② navigate: 동사 원형으로 올바름
✅ ④ potentially: 부사로 올바름
det.tip: 병렬 구조: some consciously and some unconsciously — 둘 다 부사

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ stressing → stressed: ‘you are stressed’(스트레스를 받은 상태)가 올바름. stressing은 ‘스트레스를 주는’
det.analysis:
❌ ③ stressing: 원문은 stressed(과거분사/형용사 ‘스트레스 받은’). ‘감정’ 형용사는 -ed 형태
✅ ① having: think of A as B 구문에서 동명사 올바름
✅ ② that: 관계대명사 — 선행사 self-talk 수식
✅ ④ tainted: 수동태(be tainted by) 올바름
det.tip: 감정 형용사: stressed(스트레스 받은) vs stressing(스트레스 주는)

Automatic thoughts that relieve anxiety ③<u>goes</u> something like this: You walk into a room, see a few new people, and say to yourself, “Oh, no.” They can turn a potentially good experience into one ④<u>fraught</u> with anxiety.

det.korean: ③ goes → go: 주어가 ‘Automatic thoughts that relieve anxiety’(복수)이므로 복수 동사 go가 필요
det.analysis:
❌ ③ goes: 주어 thoughts(복수) → go가 올바름. that relieve anxiety는 수식절

det.tip: 수일치: 주어 핵심 명사가 복수(thoughts)면 복수 동사(go). 관계절(that~)에 속지 말 것

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에는 restructure(재구성하다)가 적절. 부정적 사고를 바꿔야 한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ① restructure: 사고방식을 재구성하라는 문맥에 부합
❌ ② reinforce: 강화하다 — 부정적 사고를 강화하라는 뜻이 되어 부적절
❌ ③ eliminate: 제거하다 — 사고 자체를 없앤다는 극단적 표현
❌ ④ memorize: 암기하다 — 문맥에 무관
det.tip: restructure = re(다시) + structure(구조화하다) = 재구성하다

det.analysis:
✅ ③ fraught: fraught with anxiety — 불안으로 가득 찬
❌ ① satisfied: 만족한 — anxiety와 어울리지 않음
❌ ② compatible: 양립 가능한 — 문맥에 부적합
❌ ④ familiar: 익숙한 — 문맥에 부적합
det.tip: fraught with = ~로 가득 찬(주로 부정적). fraught with danger/anxiety

자동적 사고는 완전히 제거할 수 있다.

questions.passage: On the surface are your automatic thoughts. These are like short tapes that momentarily flash through your mind. Call these automatic thoughts a form of “self-talk” that you use as you navigate through the day. You produce a wide variety of these automatic thoughts, some consciously and some unconsciously. Automatic thoughts are bad habits that cloud fresh and positive experiences. They can turn a potentially good experience into one fraught with anxiety. If you tell yourself that you are always stressed or full of anxiety before doing something new, that new experience will be tainted by that anxiety.
questions.stem:
위 글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?

"Automatic thoughts, a form of (A)__________, can (B)__________ positive experiences by filling them with anxiety."

det.korean: (A) self-talk, (B) cloud/taint — 자동적 사고는 자기 대화의 한 형태로 긍정적 경험을 흐리게 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) self-talk – (B) cloud: 본문 내용과 정확히 일치
❌ ① (A) deep thinking – (B) enhance: 자동적 사고는 깊은 사고가 아니며 enhance는 반대
❌ ② (A) self-talk – (B) enhance: cloud가 아닌 enhance는 반대
❌ ④ (A) meditation – (B) cloud: 명상은 본문에 없음
det.tip: 요약문 완성: 빈칸에 본문의 핵심 키워드를 넣되 패러프레이징에 주의

questions.stem:
다음 조건에 맞게 영어 문장을 완성하시오.

"당신이 새로운 것을 하기 전에 항상 스트레스를 받는다고 자신에게 말한다면"

If you __________ that you are always stressed before doing something new

det.korean: 정답: tell yourself — ‘자신에게 말하다’ = tell yourself
det.analysis: tell yourself that ~ = 자신에게 ~라고 말하다. 재귀대명사 yourself 필수.
det.tip: tell oneself = 자신에게 말하다. say to oneself도 같은 의미
